_about: Settings for the Routes page (engine/routes/: build.py, page.html), at /toronto/routes/: pick a stop near you, see where each route from it goes. Everything Toronto-specific lives here: which modes to include, the street grid's tilt, the regions a trip is described by, the extra landmarks and the page's wording. The engine names no city.
_modes: Route modes from raw/surface/routes.json to include: bus now; add "tram" for streetcars.
_gridTilt: Degrees the street grid is turned from true north (Toronto's grid runs about 17 degrees west of north), so Yonge reads as north-south and Bloor as east-west.
_regions: Published files, in order, whose names describe where a trip goes (the first that contains a spot wins): Downtown, Midtown, East End..., then the former cities (Scarborough, North York...).

page.title: Where does my bus go?
page.description: Find the bus stops nearest you in Toronto and see where each bus goes: the neighbourhoods it passes through, the main streets it runs along, the subway stations it connects to and the landmarks on the way.
page.lede: Find the stops near you, then pick a bus to see where it goes: the neighbourhoods, main streets, subway connections and landmarks along the way.
page.outside: That spot is outside Toronto. Try an address in the city.
page.noMatch: No match in Toronto for “{q}”. Try the full street name, like “789 Yonge Street”.
page.noStops: No bus stops within {r} of that spot.
page.credits: Routes and stops: TTC (Toronto Transit Commission) schedule data via City of Toronto Open Data · Boundaries and streets: City of Toronto Open Data
